title: Prediction: UPS Will Miss Estimates (but the Stock Could Still Be a Good Value)
author: Lee Samaha
description: UPS faces headwinds from elevated fuel costs, Amazon's new supply chain services, and declining e-commerce demand, which could lead to missed earnings estimates in Q3 2026. However, the stock's high dividend yield and market expectations of a miss may position it for recovery if the company merely meets expectations. The dividend sustainability remains a concern despite the potential value opportunity.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Article predicts UPS will miss Q3 earnings estimates due to elevated fuel costs that exceed surcharge increases, competition from Amazon Supply Chain Services, and declining e-commerce demand (down 7% YOY). Dividend sustainability is questioned given the tight coverage ratio of 6.56 dividend per share against expected 7.20 EPS for 2026.

Amazon is mentioned as a competitive threat to UPS through its newly launched Supply Chain Services targeting SMB deliveries. However, the article presents this as a potential headwind for UPS rather than making a direct investment recommendation about Amazon itself.

Delta is cited as a comparable example of a company that missed estimates and cut guidance due to higher fuel expenses, with the market showing modest decline. Used as a reference point to suggest UPS stock may be similarly positioned for recovery.

title: Delta Air Lines Cuts 2026 Earnings Outlook: Time to Sell DAL Stock?
author: Na
description: Delta Air Lines has lowered its 2026 earnings guidance to $5.10-$5.60 per share from $6.50-$7.50, citing surging fuel expenses and rising operating costs. Q3 fuel costs surged 62% to $4.14B, compressing operating margins to 9.4%. Despite strong passenger demand and premium revenue growth, weakening free cash flow and negative earnings revisions raise concerns about the airline's profitability outlook.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Significant earnings guidance reduction, 62% surge in fuel expenses, 170 basis point margin contraction, declining free cash flow ($463M vs $833M YoY), and 19.72% downward earnings revision over 60 days. Zacks Rank #5 (Strong Sell) rating indicates weak near-term investment appeal despite strong demand.

Operates in the same fuel-sensitive airline industry facing elevated fuel costs and margin pressures similar to Delta. Expected to report Q3 results on Oct. 20 with anticipated negative impact from high fuel prices.

Faces identical industry headwinds as Delta and United, including fuel-cost sensitivity and operating expense inflation. Expected to report Q3 results on Oct. 22 with anticipated challenges from elevated fuel environment.

title: Should You Invest in the U.S. Global Jets ETF (JETS)?

description: The U.S. Global Jets ETF (JETS) offers exposure to global airline companies with a 0.6% expense ratio and $778.07 million in assets. title: Greg Abel Is Reshaping Berkshire's Portfolio. Here's Who's In and Who's Out.
author: Bram Berkowitz
description: Greg Abel, nine months into his tenure as Berkshire Hathaway CEO, is reshaping the company's $350 billion equities portfolio. He has designated Apple, American Express, Coca-Cola, and Moody's as core holdings with limited activity expected. Meanwhile, Abel has significantly increased positions in Alphabet (now 10.6% of portfolio), initiated new stakes in Delta Airlines, and increased exposure to housing through Lennar. Energy holdings like Chevron and Occidental Petroleum remain uncommitted, while Bank of America has been slightly trimmed. Abel has also resumed share repurchases after years of pause.

title: Archer Aviation vs. Joby Aviation: Which EV Airplane Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
author: Brendan Coffey
description: Both Archer Aviation and Joby Aviation are developing electric vertical takeoff and landing (eVTOL) aircraft for commercial use, but face significant financial challenges with massive operating losses and negative cash flows. Joby is recommended as the better buy due to its lower valuation multiple (46x P/S vs. 546x), early revenue generation from its Blade acquisition, and more advanced manufacturing capabilities, though both remain highly speculative investments with substantial regulatory and execution risks.

Recommended as the better buy with more attractive valuation (46x P/S), early revenue generation ($53.4M from Blade acquisition), advanced manufacturing capabilities using Toyota philosophies, successful real-world testing in NYC, and integrated partnerships with Delta and L3Harris, despite significant losses ($930M) and legal challenges.
